newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica sets partial privatisations to pay debt.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica sets partial privatisations to pay debt.

text.p: President Jose Maria Figueres announced Monday a package of partial sales of state assets aimed at reducing Costa Rica's internal debt burden.
Figueres said his government would end its monopoly on insurance, sell part of the state telecommunications monopoly, and seek to issue new debt.
He also said the government would continue efforts to find a buyer for Banco Internacional de Costa Rica (BICSA), currently owned by three other state banks.
The sale of BICSA was announced by the government earlier this year.
The decisions are "aimed at contributing to solve the problem of internal debt," Figueres said in a nationally-televised speech.
He said the country's internal debt is set to hit $3.5 billion at the end of this year.
He said he would sell 40 percent of the National Insurance Institute, and would sell control of the firm Radiografica Costarricense, a unit of the state Costa Rica Electricity Institute.
The government would also seek parliamentary permission to issue $200 million in debt and limit further debt issuance by the government, he said.
It would also scrap plans to lower value-added tax to 13 percent from 15 percent next year, he said, will increase certain car taxes and will freeze certain import duties at 20 percent.
